title: A long unbroken word in a record (45+ characters) makes Alerts, the aircraft list, Costs, Discrepancies and the Flight log wider than a phone, and pushes the bottom navigation off-screen
steps: 1. Phone 390x844, demo. 2. Inspections > Details on the first inspection. 3. Type 60 characters with no spaces or hyphens in Reference (the field accepts 2,000) and Save inspection. 4. Open /alerts, then /aircraft. Same result with: a member name of 45+ unbroken characters on /discrepancies ('Reported by ...') and /flights; an aircraft model of 45+ unbroken characters in the aircraft select on /costs; a long inspection Description on /alerts.
expected: The text wraps or truncates inside its card; the page stays 390px wide and the five bottom-navigation items stay on screen.
actual: /alerts is 1022px wide and /aircraft 854px wide (8020px and 6724px with 500 characters). The fixed bottom bar stretches with the page, so 2-3 of its 5 items (Log flight, Inspections, More) are off-screen until the user scrolls sideways. Desktop 1440 also scrolls sideways at 500 characters (/alerts 8316px, /aircraft 7078px, /discrepancies 1877px).
evidence: shots/ui-long-inspref-alerts-phone.png, shots/ui-long-inspref-aircraft-phone.png, shots/ui-long-member-discrepancies-phone.png, shots/ui-long-model-costs-phone.png; src/styles/screens/dashboard.css:575 (.dash-status-reasons li), src/styles/screens/shop.css:370 (.shop-select), src/components/Records.tsx:885
suspect: src/styles/screens/dashboard.css:585 and the alert row title / .rec reporter line / .shop-select select: no overflow-wrap:anywhere or min-width:0/max-width:100% on these text containers
notes: The 3 Nov hunt reported 'no horizontal overflow on 28 routes' with seed data only. A single long flight Origin, Remarks or Discrepancy (500 chars, saved through the flight form) does NOT overflow: those wrap correctly. Hyphenated text also wraps. Repro files are .cjs because the scratchpad has a package.json with type=module.

title: The Inventory location select in New parts / repair request has no accessible name (axe critical: select-name)
steps: 1. /parts-requests > New request. 2. Run axe-core on the dialog, or inspect the select under the 'Inventory location' label.
expected: The select is announced as 'Inventory location' and clicking the label focuses it, like every other field in the dialog.
actual: <label for="_r_x_">Inventory location</label> points at an id that no element has; the <select> has no id, aria-label or wrapping label. axe: select-name (critical) on '.field:nth-child(4) > select'. A screen reader announces only 'combo box'. axe also reports scrollable-region-focusable (serious) on .request-availability at phone width in the same dialog.
suspect: src/components/ui.tsx:179 (Field only clones a single element child; LocationField passes the select plus a conditional <small>, so children is an array and the id is never applied)
notes: Same two-children pattern at src/components/PlanComponentMovement.tsx:281-283 (input name=reference plus <small>); not opened in the browser, check it with the fix. All 48 other first-level dialogs passed axe serious/critical in phone-light and desktop-dark.

title: A decimal comma or a missed decimal point in Ending Hobbs (2342,5 -> 23425) is accepted as a 21,083.8-hour flight with no warning, which rewrites the aircraft total and grounds it
steps: 1. Chromium, English (US) locale, demo, phone or desktop. 2. Flight log > Log a completed flight (N206MA, starting Hobbs 2341.2). 3. Type 2342,5 in Ending Hobbs: the field silently drops the comma and shows 23425 (typing 23425 for 2342.5 gives the same). 4. Save flight.
expected: The form refuses or asks the pilot to confirm an implausible flight time (the form itself shows 'Flight time · Hobbs 21083.8 h'), or the entry is held for administrator review like a reading that is lower than the counter.
actual: 'Entry synchronized successfully.' The flight is accepted; N206MA total becomes 23,425.0 h, the 100-hour inspection shows '21,075.0 h overdue' and the aircraft shows Grounded. Every hours-based due figure for the aircraft is now wrong until an administrator finds and corrects the flight. A reading 341 h too LOW is held for review; a reading 21,000 h too HIGH is not.
evidence: shots/ui-flightform-comma-typed-phone.png, shots/ui-flightform-comma-dashboard-phone.png; src/domain/flights.ts:185-217 (conflictReason has only lower-than-counter checks); src/components/FlightForm.tsx:895-899 (type=number, inputMode=decimal, no max)
suspect: src/domain/flights.ts:185 (no upper plausibility rule) and src/components/FlightForm.tsx:895 (number input with no max relative to the starting reading and no confirmation for a long flight)
notes: Proven in the demo; the same shared rule (conflictReason) runs on the server, and no convex test was written here: the flights tester may cover the server side. The comma is dropped by Chromium for an English-locale number input; a browser set to a comma-decimal locale parses it correctly, so the realistic triggers are (a) a pilot used to comma decimals on an English-locale device and (b) a missed decimal point on a phone keypad. Tach has the same field type. Owner decision: what counts as implausible (e.g. more than 24 h in one flight) and whether to block, confirm or hold for review.

title: Escape or the browser/phone Back button closes a filled-in flight, inspection completion, work order or discrepancy form without asking and the typed data is lost
steps: 1. Demo, phone. 2. Overview > Flight log > Log a completed flight. 3. Type an ending Hobbs and remarks. 4. Press the browser Back button (the Android back gesture) or Escape. 5. Open the form again.
expected: The app asks before discarding typed data (as the checklist editor does: 'Discard unsaved checklist changes?'), or keeps a draft and restores it.
actual: The form closes at once with no question (Back also leaves the Flight log for the previous page). Reopened, every field is empty. Same for Inspections > Complete, Work orders > Open work order and Discrepancies > Report a problem. Clicking outside the dialog does not close it (good).
evidence: work/ui/unsaved.cjs output (12 cases: escape and back close with no confirm on all four forms; scrim click keeps the dialog); src/components/ChecklistEditor.tsx:82,141 is the only editor with a dirty check; src/components/design.tsx:961-970 (onCancel closes unconditionally)
suspect: src/components/design.tsx:961 (useDismiss closes on cancel with no dirty guard) and the route change unmounting open dialogs
notes: The guided Start flight / End flight path keeps its state in localStorage and was not affected. On a phone the Back gesture inside a full-screen sheet is the usual way people try to close it, so a pilot or mechanic can lose a long entry (inspection completion wording, discrepancy text) with one swipe.

title: User-facing text says 'reminders' and 'notification' where the glossary requires 'alert', and the board summary PDF prints '1 open discrepancies'
steps: 1. Settings (and Airworthiness > FAA connection and renewal settings): read the FAA key panel. 2. Save any flight; inspect the close button of the 'Entry synchronized successfully.' notice. 3. Board view > Download board summary (PDF) with one open discrepancy on an aircraft.
expected: 'alert' wording per GLOSSARY.md (Alert: avoid notification, reminder; Expiring date: avoid reminder); '1 open discrepancy'.
actual: 'Renewal reminders appear here and on the overview starting 60 days before expiry'; after replacing the key: 'Replacement key verified with FAA and saved. Renewal reminder updated.'; the notice close button's accessible name is 'Dismiss notification'; the PDF line reads 'N208MA (Cessna 208 Caravan): Airworthy. 0 overdue, 0 due soon. 1 open discrepancies.'
evidence: src/components/FaaKeySettings.tsx:84,97; src/App.tsx (Notice, aria-label="Dismiss notification"); src/data/boardSummaryPdf.ts:75; work/ui/pdf/board-summary.pdf; GLOSSARY.md:202-212
notes: May overlap the generic known item E-15 (small wording errors); listed because these three are concrete. The repro covers the two on-screen strings and the button name; the PDF plural was read from the downloaded file.

title: The desktop sidebar brand link's accessible name ('Angel One overview') does not contain its visible text 'AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS' (axe serious: label-content-name-mismatch, every route)
steps: 1. Desktop 1440x900, any route. 2. Run axe-core 4.x with default rules.
expected: The visible label is part of the accessible name (WCAG 2.5.3), so speech-control users can say what they see.
actual: axe reports label-content-name-mismatch (serious) on '.brand' on all 31 routes in light and dark, and in the owner portal and board view previews. It is the only serious/critical axe result on any route at phone and desktop sizes in both themes.
notes: The 3 Nov hunt recorded axe as clean; this rule may be newer in the axe-core version used here (latest from npm on 10 Nov).

title: The Record history panel in the inspection Complete and Details dialogs shows a red 'History not found.' error and a 'Load more' button when the record has no change-log entries yet
steps: 1. Demo, Inspections. 2. Click Complete (or Details) on any seeded inspection. 3. Scroll to RECORD HISTORY under the form.
expected: An empty state such as 'No changes recorded yet.' and no Load more button; an error style only when loading really failed.
actual: A red error box 'History not found.' with a 'Load more' button, directly under the Record completion button, so a mechanic signing off an inspection sees an error before saving anything.
evidence: shots/ui-history-not-found-inspection-complete.png; src/data/demoBackend.ts:1102-1103; src/domain/auditHistory.ts:61-73 (canPageAuditFilter is false when the record has no newest entry and is not in the scope list); convex/auditHistory.ts:199-214 uses the same rule; src/components/ManagementShared.tsx (Record history panel)
suspect: src/domain/auditHistory.ts:61 (no entries is treated the same as not visible) and the panel in src/components/ManagementShared.tsx rendering the refusal as an error
notes: Confirmed in the demo, where the seeded inspections have no audit rows. The server calls the same shared rule, so a live record with no audit rows (legacy import, or the imports in known item RM-44) should show the same error; that was not run against convex-test here. Related to known RM-59 (demo differs from server) only if the server turns out to behave differently.

title: The server accepts a flight whose ending Hobbs is 10x the aircraft's current reading (a 21,070-hour flight) and applies it to the aircraft totals: no plausibility guard in the form, the domain or the server
steps: 1. Copy repro/ui/zz-hunt-ui8-server-hobbs-jump.test.ts to convex/. 2. npx vitest run convex/zz-hunt-ui8-server-hobbs-jump.test.ts. It submits api.operations.submit kind=flight with hobbsOn = currentHobbs*10 (2341.2 h -> 23412 h), then one with currentHobbs + 100.1 h.
expected: A flight far longer than any real flight is refused or held for review (status 'review', totals unchanged), the way a reading below the counter is.
actual: Both flights are stored with status 'accepted' and aircraft.currentHobbs becomes 84,283,200 s (23,412 h) / +100.1 h. Both tests fail (2 failed). validateFlight only checks the required meter and a future start time; conflictReason only checks version, chronology and readings LOWER than the counter.
evidence: vitest output: 'the flight was accepted into aircraft totals: expected [ {...} ] to have a length of +0 but got 1' and 'expected 8788680 to be 8428320'; src/domain/flights.ts:161-172 (validateFlight), src/domain/flights.ts:185-217 (conflictReason), src/domain/model.ts:168 (meterReadingSchema)
suspect: src/domain/flights.ts:185 (conflictReason has no upper bound on the jump from the current counter)
notes: This is the server half of UI-3: the browser slip (decimal comma dropped, missed decimal point) is not caught anywhere downstream. Owner decision: the limit (for example more than 24 h or more than 100 h in one entry) and whether to refuse or hold for review. Tach, collective hourmeter and flight time log go through the same rule.

title: Every type=number field silently drops a typed or pasted decimal comma (2341,2 becomes 23412), and the aircraft form saves the 10x reading as the aircraft's current Hobbs without a question
steps: 1. Chromium, English (US). 2. Aircraft > Edit aircraft (N206MA). 3. Clear Current Hobbs (hours), type 2341,2: the field shows 23412. 4. Save aircraft.
expected: The comma is refused with a message, or read as a decimal; a meter reading 10x the previous one asks for confirmation.
actual: 'Change saved.' N206MA currentHobbs is stored as 23,412 h (baseline 2341.2). The same dropped comma was measured on all 50 number fields probed. STORED 10x with no guard: flight Ending Hobbs / Ending Tach (UI-3, UI-8), aircraft form and setup wizard Current Hobbs, Current tach, Current landings, flight fuel and oil (UI-11). REFUSED by a later rule: inspection Complete 'Tracked total at completion' ('Compliance readings must be between last compliance and current aircraft totals.'), flight Landings (max 1000), Warn days before (max 730), engine trend limits (min/max). NOT saved in this round (control accepts 23425, storage not checked): component TSN/TSO/TSR and cycles at install, aircraft total time and cycles at install, inspection 'Repeat every (hours)', 'Last complied at', 'One-time due', job card Actual labor (hours), calendar months since new/overhaul, PDF page number.
evidence: work/ui/nums.json (53 fields x 11 probes, typed and pasted); work/ui/store2-aircraft.log; shots/ui-num-aircraft-edit.png; src/components/Fleet.tsx:558,624,690,701; src/components/FlightForm.tsx:895
suspect: shared: number inputs have min=0 but no max tied to the current reading, and no form checks the size of the jump (src/components/Fleet.tsx:558, src/components/FlightForm.tsx:895, src/components/Components.tsx:622)
notes: Other probes on the same fields: '2,342.5' -> 2342.5 (correct); '2342.5 h' -> 2342.5 (units dropped, correct value); ' 12 ' -> 12; '+5' -> 5; '-5' blocked by min=0 except 'Total time adjustment (hours)' which has no min by design; '1e5' stays in the control and is refused on hours fields by parseHours ('Use positive hours with at most one decimal place.') but stored on step=any fields (UI-11); an empty required field is blocked by the browser; 999999999999 is accepted by every meter field (no max). '2.342,5' -> 2.3425, blocked by step=0.1 on meter fields. Pasting behaves the same as typing on these fields. A browser set to a comma-decimal locale parses the comma correctly.

title: Money fields strip every comma, so a decimal comma is stored 100x too large (labor rate 45,50 is saved as $4,550.00 per hour)
steps: 1. Settings > labor rate: type 45,50 in 'Rate per hour (USD)' and press Enter.
expected: '45,50' is refused ('Enter a positive amount with up to two decimals.') or read as 45.50; only a comma followed by three digits is treated as a thousands separator.
actual: Saved with no message; costs settings laborRateCents = 455000 ($4,550.00/h), which then prices every labor entry that uses the program rate. parseCents removes all commas before validating. Same parser: Costs '<year> budget (USD)', work order expense 'amount', work order labor 'rate'. Other probes on the rate field: '2,342.5' -> $2,342.50 (correct); ' 45.5 ' and '$45.50' -> $45.50; '1.234,56', '1e3', '+45', '-45', '45.5 USD' -> refused with 'Enter a positive amount with up to two decimals.'; 999999 -> 'Amount is too large.'
notes: Only the Settings rate was saved in the browser; the budget and work order fields were read in code (same parseCents call) and not driven.

title: Flight fuel and oil fields store whatever the number control holds: 2.342,5 as 2.3425, 1e5 as 100,000 gal, 0,5 qt as 5 qt, with no plausibility check
steps: 1. Flight log > Log a completed flight, valid ending Hobbs. 2. Type: Fuel starting level 2.342,5; Fuel quantity added 1e5; Fuel shutdown level 45,5; Engine oil starting level 7,5; Engine oil quantity added 0,5. 3. Save flight.
expected: Values that cannot be right for the aircraft (100,000 gal added, shutdown level above start plus added, 75 qt of oil) are questioned or refused.
actual: Flight accepted; stored fuel {start: 2.3425, added: 100000, end: 455} and oil {start: 75, added: 5}. These fields are step='any', min=0, max=1000000. The same step='any' behaviour (2.342,5 accepted as 2.3425, 1e5 accepted) was measured on job card 'Actual labor (hours)' and component 'Calendar time since new/overhaul (months)', not saved.
notes: Lower severity than the meters because fuel and oil do not drive due dates, but oil added per hour is what a mechanic reads for engine health.

title: Quantity and cost fields on New parts request and New PO cannot be emptied, show a leading zero (012), and silently turn -5 and 1e5 into 5
steps: 1. Purchase orders > New PO. 2. Select all in 'Part 1 quantity' and delete: the field shows 0. 3. Type 12: it shows 012. 4. Clear, type -5: 05. 5. Clear, type 1e5: 05.
expected: The field can be empty while editing, shows what was typed, and refuses a sign or exponent visibly.
actual: Typed '' -> '0', '12' -> '012', '-5' -> '05', '1e5' -> '05'. Same on 'Shipping cost' and 'Part 1 unit cost' (step .01; '2.342,5' typed becomes 2.35, pasted becomes 2.34) and on New parts request 'Quantity'. Pasting differs from typing here: pasted '-5' -> 0, pasted '1e5' -> 01e5.
suspect: src/components/PurchaseOrders.tsx:943 (controlled number input that writes Number(value) back on every keystroke)
notes: What a PO line stores after these was not checked; the visible value is what the user will trust.
